h1: A medical product catalogue website where every product has its own page.
sub: A catalogue website is not a PDF with a download button. It is one page per product, carrying the specification table, the brochure, the applications and an enquiry form, arranged by product line so a buyer and a search engine can both find their way.
meta_ticks: One page per product, not a PDF

persona: Sales or marketing head at a medical-equipment company with several product lines and a PDF catalogue

sections.h2: What a medical product catalogue website is
paras: A medical product catalogue website turns your price list and brochure folder into a browsable structure: product lines at the top, categories under them, and a page for every individual product holding its specification table, images, applications, accessories, the brochure as a download, and an enquiry form that names the product it came from.

Because each product has a real page with real content, it can be found directly by someone searching for that model or that application, instead of being buried in a PDF that search engines cannot rank well. Where volume justifies it, the same structure carries programmatic pages per product and per city.

Elevate Aura built this structure for Medline Robotics, a medical robotics company in Chennai, alongside their storefront and distributor portal, with 253 product and city landing pages across four product lines.

sections.eyebrow: Why the PDF catalogue is costing you
sections.h2: Your whole range lives in one file nobody can search.
sections.lead: A catalogue PDF made sense when it was printed. On a website it hides every product you sell behind a single download link.

items.p: A buyer searching for a specific model finds a competitor's page rather than a page of yours, because you do not have one.
Spec tables pasted in as screenshots cannot be read, compared or indexed, and they are unreadable on a phone.
A single contact form means the sales team has to ask which product the enquiry was about before they can quote.
One changed specification means a new PDF, a new upload and old copies still circulating on WhatsApp.

sections.h2: From a price list to a structured catalogue.

steps.p: Product lines, categories and products agreed from your price list, so the URL structure mirrors how you sell.
One field set per product line, so every product in that line carries the same attributes and can be compared.
Your Excel sheet is mapped into those fields and loaded, rather than forty pages being typed by hand.
Specification table, images, applications, accessories, brochure download and a product-specific enquiry form.
Related products, accessories and the parent line are cross-linked, so a visitor moves sideways instead of leaving.
The line goes live, and product-and-city pages are added where there is real demand to justify them.

items.q: How many products can the catalogue hold?
items.a: There is no practical limit. The structure is built once per product line and products are imported from your Excel sheet, so a hundred products is data entry rather than a hundred design jobs.

items.q: Do we have to show prices?
items.a: No. Most medical catalogues show specifications and take an enquiry or quote request instead of a price. Where you do want prices, they can be shown publicly, or only to logged-in dealers at their own tier.

items.q: Can buyers still download the brochure?
items.a: Yes, per product, and you choose whether the download is open or asks for a name and number first. Each download is recorded as a GA4 event so you can see which products draw interest.

items.q: Can the catalogue become a store later?
items.a: Yes. The same product data supports a quote-to-order storefront with dealer pricing and payment verification. See medical equipment e-commerce development.
Your team, through the admin. Adding a product means filling the defined fields for that line and uploading the brochure. Bulk changes can still be done by re-importing the sheet.

items.q: Does the catalogue connect to stock?
items.a: It can. With Aura Business the catalogue reads the same product master, so a product added in operations appears on the site and enquiries land as leads.
